question.leadin: In his pseudo-historical book 1421, Gavin Menzies claimed that an explorer from this dynasty visited the Americas before Christopher Columbus.
question.text: Name this Chinese dynasty, renowned for its blue and white porcelain, which succeeded the Yuan dynasty and preceded the Qing dynasty.
question.clue: It ended when Li Zicheng mutinied and Nurhaci led an invasion force.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about weird Chinese emperors.
swap.text: This dynasty's emperor Toghon Temur once considered the idea of killing everyone with the surnames Zhang, Wang, Liu, Li, and Zhao, which would've killed more than 90% of China's population. This dynasty was established in China by Kublai Khan.
swap.clue: It ended when the Red Turban Rebellion forced Togon Temur to flee its capital of Dadu in 1368.

question.text: Rustichello da Pisa wrote a travelogue about this man's journey to China, where he lived in the court of Kublai Khan.
question.clue: Two Dominican monks and gifts from Pope Gregory X were carried east by Maffeo and Niccolo, who were this man's uncle and father, respectively.

swap.text: The Chinese Civil War resumed after World War II, and in 1949, Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists were forced to retreat to this island.
swap.clue: The 17th century Kingdom of Tungning on this island hoped to restore the Ming dynasty to power.

question.leadin: A period of the same name in China ended with the establishment of the Qin Dynasty.
question.text: Identify this time of unrest in Japanese history that began with the Onin War. It resulted in the destruction of Kyoto, the capital of the ruling Ashikaga Shogunate.
question.clue: The Hundred Schools of Thought blossomed during this period, which chronologically follows the Spring and Autumn period.

swap.text: This program of Mao's was started in order to cleanse China of supposed bourgeois threats. Students formed the Red Guard during this event, and Deng Xiaoping was imprisoned for its duration.
swap.clue: Just before this event's beginning, a February Outline was issued by the Five Man Group as a response to an accusation that a real-life house arrest was the basis of the allegedly unpatriotic drama Hai Rui Dismissed From Office.

question.leadin: The political relationships between China and Korea in the 7th century were often fractious.
question.text: This dynasty lost power after 300,000 soldiers died at the Salsu River when the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo opened the dams across it. Its first emperor, Emperor Wen, reunified China and rebuilt the Grand Canal.
question.clue: This dynasty managed to defeat the formidable war elephants of the Champa in Vietnam, and possibly one of the greatest architectural advancements during this dynasty was Emperor Wen's construction of the Grand Canal.

swap.leadin: This rebellion's eventual victor won the Battle of Lake Poyang against Chen Youliang's forces.
swap.text: Name this 14th-century rebellion initiated by Han Shantong and the White Lotus Society. This rebellion resulted in the downfall of the Yuan dynasty.
swap.clue: After its completion in 1368, this event brought about the Ming Dynasty.

question.leadin: Answer the following about leaders who worked in factories abroad during their political exile.
question.text: This man, Time's Man of the Year in both 1978 and 1985, spent time in France working in a tractor factory after falling from favor. This paramount leader introduced the "Four Modernizations" to his country's economy.
question.answerHtml: Deng Xiaoping [or Deng Xixian; or Teng Hsiao-ping; or Xiansheng; or Xixian]
question.clue: This "second generation" leader's "Southern Tour" publicized the success of the first four special economic zones he created as part of "reform and opening up."

swap.leadin: Name these areas that were once independent from China.
swap.text: The source of the Jurchen tribe who formed the last Chinese dynasty, it was made independent again under another name as a Japanese puppet state in the 1930s.
swap.clue: Imperial support of the Yehetribe in this region was cited as one of Nurhaci's (nuer-ha-chee) Seven Grievances.

question.text: The massive naval battle of Red Cliffs pitted Cao Cao ("tsao tsao") against Liu Bei ("l'yoh bay"), two veterans of a Daoist revolt against the Han named for yellow examples of these clothing items. The Yuan dynasty collapsed after revolts named for red examples of these items.
question.answerHtml: turbans [or jīn; or tóujīn accept scarves; accept Yellow Turban Rebellions or Red Turban Rebellions]
question.clue: The name for the Qizilbash refers to a distinctive type of this object they possessed.

swap.text: After the Ten Attendants were removed from power, this period of Chinese history occurred and was named for the land divided between Wei, Wu, and Shu. The Jin Dynasty succeeded this period.
swap.clue: In the lead up to this period, one side lost the Battle of Red Cliffs.

question.leadin: He shares his name with the Tang emperor who was the husband of Empress Wu and conquered Korea in 668.
question.text: Name this emperor who ruled from 1127 to 1187, using his general Yue Fei to hold off the invasions of the Juchen and fortify the southern part of the former empire.

swap.leadin: This city is home to the supertall CITIC plaza.
swap.text: Name this city, also home to a Joseph di Pasquale-designed giant "circle," the headquarter of its plastic exchange. An opera house in this city was built using a "twin-pebble design."
swap.clue: During the First Opium War, the Wellesley captured a fort on Whampoa Island near this city.

question.leadin: Answer the following about royals who were assassinated by Serbian nationalists.
question.text: The coup in which Alexander I was killed is named for this month. This month also names a series of anti-Semitic laws passed by Alexander III of Russia.
question.clue: The New York chapter of the Prairie Fire Organizing Committee was the basis for a "Communist Organization" formed by members of the Weather Underground, named for the 19th of this month.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Opium Wars.
swap.text: The First Opium War was ended by this "unequal treaty," which established treaty ports and ceded Hong Kong to Great Britain.
swap.clue: The First Opium War was ended by this treaty that ceded Hong Kong and opened other ports to the British.

question.leadin: As part of this reform, the Zongli Yamen was created to supervise foreign relations, and Li Hongzhang was given the governorship of Jiangsu with responsibility for suppressing rebellions.
question.text: Identify this cautious reform ideology which took hold in China in 1861, and sought to build up military power without compromising existing Confucian social mores.
question.clue: Its major political proponent was Prince Gong, who supported the reforms of Zuo Zongtang, Li Hongzhang, and Zeng Guofan.

swap.leadin: This man started the practice of regional militia armies in his native Hunan province, and that practice would later spread under his proteges Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang.
swap.text: Name this Chinese general and statesman who led the successful campaign to reclaim Nanjing and is credited with suppressing the Taiping Rebellion.
swap.clue: As part of his work as a leader in the Self-Strengthening Movement, he founded the Shanghai Arsenal.

question.text: The Tang Dynasty came to an end after a peasant uprising started by this man and Wang Xianzhi. He captured Changan but was betrayed by his general Zhu Wen, who in turn deposed the last Tang emperor.

swap.leadin: Answer questions about historically significant gates.
swap.text: The "Incident at Xuanwu Gate" saw this ruler take power by ambushing and killing his brother Li Jiangcheng. This ruler succeeded Gaozu, or Li Yuan, as the second emperor of the Tang Dynasty.
swap.clue: This man who ruled from 976 to 997 and extinguished the Northern Han to bring to a final end the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms.
